compatibilityEvidence.claim: Scarce/costly observation can make evidence selection strategically consequential.
Abundant evidence can collapse epistemic play toward checklist completion when access choices no longer matter.
Constrained drafting plus synergies can create path-dependent global decisions that outperform local greedy choice.
Changing production goals can move bottlenecks and force different architectures under shared capacity constraints.
Sparse interaction plus compounding is insufficient when most states preserve one strong upgrade order.
Creation choices become strategically differentiated when the audience has hidden but learnable responsive preferences.
Responsive-other value does not by itself establish a need for LLM/model cognition; deterministic policy already produced the tested distinction.
Visible telegraphs add little depth when changing them rarely changes the best action.
Delegation can produce distinct outcomes but creates interpretation/review cost; it needs enough strategic leverage to repay administration burden.
Hidden state becomes playable when player-legible evidence supports model formation and revision.
Live-model testimony did not outperform a cheaper fixed/policy testimony baseline in the tested Casefile slice.
Richer cognition is not automatically needed for adaptive opposition when a cheap policy produces similar player trajectories.
Resource optimization can dominate a relationship treatment and prevent clean inference about trust/dependency value.
Automation plus legible bottlenecks may shift player work from repetition toward diagnosis and architecture.
Telegraphing, commitment/recovery windows and cheap retry may form a mastery loop when failure is attributable.
Self-authored goals plus persistent world transformation may support ownership and authorship.
Mechanically distinct approaches may feel more agentic when later state/relationships acknowledge the consequence.
A stable action grammar can remain variable when goals, blockers and scarcity repeatedly change local action value.
Spatially embodied timing plus immediate feedback may strengthen motor learning and anticipation.
Mastery and comeback volatility may coexist in short social races, but fairness/noise tradeoffs require Human evidence.
One-life stakes and uncertain resources may increase route/engagement consequence.
Persistent place transformation plus real-time change may support attachment and return rhythms.
Role asymmetry plus team objectives and power curves may create delayed interdependence.
Incomplete information plus lethal/short-round team structure may make spatial mistakes and information work consequential.
Multiple verbs coupled through a shared responsive world may create improvised cross-system plans.
